A hectic round roundup
The main theme was treat supplies

The month stayed busy, but the Companion Animal Travel Desk kept service steady and friendly across booking, check-in, and arrival support. The team stayed close to travelers and pets, and that helped reduce last-minute confusion. Communication with ground staff was clear, and the handoff process felt smoother than it did earlier in the season.

Operationally, the senior coordinator kept daily decisions moving with a calm hand, while the safety coordinator stayed focused on hazard checks and prevention. The welcome team did a good job preparing passengers for boarding, especially when pets were nervous or owners needed a quick reminder on paperwork and carrier readiness. <<FACT F049>> The work was practical, patient, and very hands-on, which is exactly what this desk needs.

We also saw good attention to cabin planning and support resources. <<FACT F031>> That kind of structure helped the desk manage expectations more cleanly and avoid avoidable delays. Treat restocks held up well overall, though we still need to watch supply balance closely so the welcome kits stay consistent and easy to grab.

A few travelers stood out for how smoothly their trips went, including families who arrived prepared and followed guidance without fuss. Ranger had a calm trip through the process, and that kind of easy flow is always good for the whole desk. The team kept notes current, followed up on small concerns, and stayed flexible when plans shifted.

Next month, we will keep tightening prep checks, watch supply use more carefully, and keep the warm tone that passengers respond to best.
